note: Load-level IVSC v1 vectors (plan 03-11, D-34): layer 2 of ivs_machine_load against the profile's cartridge span. Every byte is authored for this project. A record names segments, not bytes: the test assembles the container (prefix, entries, generated 10-bit words), seals it with the core SHA-256 at test time and loads it on a fresh instance of the profile below, asserting status, report detail, whole-storage equality and the state digest. Span-relative addresses (span_lo, span_hi) are resolved by cmake/IvsCartTable.cmake from the cart row of data/memmap/<profile>.literal.txt, never typed in. Code-built cases of the suite: ivsc.L07-second-load-duplicate, ivsc.L08-null-args, ivsc.L09-unload-restores, ivsc.L10-two-instances, ivsc.B07-load-out-of-span, ivsc.X01-span-matches-map.

fixtures.note: One word on the last word of the cartridge span: inside, so the load is OK.

Two words from the last word of the span: the second is one word past it. On this profile the span ends at FFFF, so the parser's address-wrap rule refuses it first (the generator checks the reason against the resolved span).
One word starting one word below the span: layer 2 refuses it.
One word at 0100, in the scratchpad range below the span.
One word at 1000, the EXEC range.
Two words starting one word below the span start: the segment straddles it.
One word at 0200, the system RAM range.
Four words at the span start in a container requiring feature bit 0, which the profile does not support.
Four words at the span start in a container requiring feature bit 31.
